title: openai-agents 0.21.1 vs langgraph 1.2.11, gpt-4o

environment.note: CX23 unavailable in all six datacenters; cpx11 is the largest option strictly under the approved ceiling. Never upgraded.

model.endpoint_note: openai-agents defaults to the Responses API; it was forced to Chat Completions so both arms hit the same endpoint. Disclosed on the page.

subject.tracing: disabled three ways (OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING, set_tracing_disabled, no-op processor); default is on and uploads prompts and tool payloads to api.openai.com/v1/traces/ingest

control.tracing: off by default; LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2 unset, LANGSMITH_TRACING=false
control.role: same-day control, re-measured from scratch; not comparable to the published 1.2.9 numbers

shared.isolation: two pip-less, hash-verified virtualenvs; network blocked except api.openai.com

design.task_suite_frozen: verified unchanged against the gpt4o pilot manifest before warmup
design.order: counterbalanced; even run indexes run the subject first, odd the control

results_summary.failures: zero in both arms; the failure taxonomy is empty for this run

known_limitations: One model only (gpt-4o). The comparison holds for this model; it is not a general claim.
The subject is OpenAI's own SDK benchmarked on an OpenAI model. The same-day control and the published raw data are the answer; the page should name the objection.
openai-agents 0.21.1 was one day old at measurement time.
Both arms forced onto Chat Completions; the subject ships defaulting to Responses. Latency as-shipped may differ.

Zero failures means the failure taxonomy has no data this run; the divergence found in fake-mode acceptance tests (openai-agents rejects malformed tool arguments as malformed_tool_call, LangGraph coerces and fails later as invalid_final_answer) is an adapter-test finding, not a scored-run finding.
